title: Grain marketing and tax timing across December 31
text: Tools available to a cash-basis Saskatchewan grain/cattle sole proprietor (all law unless noted): 1. Sale timing: income is recognized when payment is received (s.28(1)(a)). Delivering grain on contract in December but taking payment in January moves income to 2027. Payment received in December (cheque or e-transfer) is 2026 income regardless of delivery date. 2. Deferred cash purchase tickets (s.76(4)): wheat, oats, barley, rye, flaxseed, rapeseed/canola delivered to a licensed primary or process elevator with an interest-free ticket payable after year-end are included in the following year. Not available for pulses, soybeans or specialty crops. 3. Prepaying inputs (s.28(1)(e),(e.1)): payments for inventory (seed, fertilizer, chemical, feed) are deductible when paid, subject to the MIA if a loss results. Prepaid non-inventory expenses (rent, insurance, service contracts) are deductible only for the current and immediately following year; a prepayment covering two or more years ahead is deducted in the year it relates to. 4. Inventory adjustments (s.28(1)(b),(c)): the OIA can increase 2026 income (up to inventory FMV less MIA) to use low brackets, and reverses as a deduction in 2027. 5. CCA: optional - claim less in low-income years. 6. Livestock deferral (s.80.3) only in prescribed regions (RM 428 was prescribed for 2025, not on the initial 2026 list). 7. AgriInvest Fund 2 withdrawals, AgriStability and crop insurance payments are income when received - schedule withdrawals into lower-income years. 8. APP cash advances are loans, not income: borrow against stored grain to fund 2026 expenses while selling in 2027. Income bunching risk: deferral is not elimination. Rolling deferrals year over year pile income into a future year (e.g., retirement, death, incorporation, a forced sale in a market spike). Each year's target should be to fill the lower brackets (2026: 14%/10.5% to $54,532-$58,523; 33% combined to $117,045; 38.5% to $155,805) rather than minimize tax in one year. Consider CCB and OAS income tests, RRSP earned-income room, and CPP pensionable earnings when choosing the target. Instalments: the December 31 farmer instalment (2/3 of estimated tax or prior-year base) must be set at the same time as the year-end marketing decisions. Common mistakes: post-dating cheques with a non-licensed buyer and calling it a cash ticket; prepaying three years of land rent; deferring so much that the next year jumps to 47.5%; forgetting the MIA on prepaid fertilizer in a loss year.

title: Proposed or announced measures not yet law (as of 2026-10-23)
text: This entry lists measures relevant to the farm household that were announced but, on the evidence reviewed, are not confirmed as enacted. Treat as "proposed" until confirmed. 1. Bovine tuberculosis compensation deferral (AAFC, March 2026): the government "intends to propose" amending s.80.3 so producers in Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba who received Health of Animals Act compensation in 2025 or 2026 for the 2024-2025 bovine TB events can spread inclusion: at least 83% in 2027 (up to 100% deferred to 2027), at least 9% in 2028, at least 4% in 2029, remaining 4% in 2030. Status: proposed; no bill identified. 2. Spring Economic Update 2026: now LAW, enacted in Bill C-30 (Royal Assent June 19, 2026): the Home Buyers' Plan repayment grace period extended to first withdrawals through 2028; the labour mobility deduction for tradespeople raised to $10,000 for 2026 (120 km test); the permanent $10 million capital gains exemption on sales to employee ownership trusts; the federal excise tax on gasoline and diesel at $0.00 from April 20 to September 7, 2026; immediate expensing for greenhouse buildings. The same Act cuts the CPP base contribution rate from 9.9% to 9.5% starting in 2027 (self-employed pay both shares), which lowers a farmer's CPP cost from 2027. Still to confirm: the Disability Tax Credit certification changes and immediate expensing for manufacturing and processing buildings. 3. Agricultural cooperative patronage dividends paid in shares: Budget 2025 extends the tax deferral to shares issued before the end of 2030 (status of enactment not confirmed in this review). Relevant if receiving patronage shares from a co-op (e.g., Federated Co-op/inputs). 4. LCGE indexation: enacted (Bill C-15); CRA shows $1,275,000 for 2026. 5. Canada Carbon Rebate for Small Businesses: non-taxability announced June 2025 via draft legislation; confirm enactment before amending returns. 6. Livestock tax deferral 2026 list: initial list (September 1, 2026) has no Saskatchewan regions; additions may be announced later in 2026 - monitor AAFC. Confirmed law (for contrast): lowest federal rate 14% (C-4, March 12, 2026); consumer carbon charge removed (C-4); AII/RIIP reinstatement and immediate expensing for Classes 43, 43.1, 54-56 (C-15, March 26, 2026); LCGE $1.25M (C-15); capital gains inclusion stays at 1/2 (increase cancelled March 21, 2025); Top-Up Tax Credit 2025-2030 (C-15).
